title: Linkability of assignment metadata
description: Metadata in the data flow (student ID, course, timestamp) could be linked with other data sources to create a comprehensive profile of the student's academic activities and patterns.

title: Identifiability of student in transit
description: The combination of student ID, course, and submission timestamp in the data flow could be used to uniquely identify the student, potentially exposing their identity to unauthorized observers.

title: Disclosure of assignment content in transit
description: The work file being transmitted could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to unauthorized access to the student's assignment content.

title: Usurpation of student identity
description: The student could be impersonated during login or submission if authentication credentials are compromised, allowing unauthorized individuals to submit assignments on their behalf.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of stored assignment data
description: The Grades Portal Web App could store assignment data in a way that allows unauthorized access or disclosure to third parties, including other students, administrators, or external systems.

title: Lack of non-repudiation for submission
description: Without proper audit trails and cryptographic signatures, the student could potentially deny submitting an assignment, or the system could deny that a specific student submitted it.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Student ID, course, file reference, and role data transmitted between portal and grading service could be intercepted if not properly encrypted, enabling unauthorized identification of students.

title: Linkability via Metadata
description: Metadata in the data flow (student ID, course, file reference) could be used to link multiple data points and identify students across different systems or time periods.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure at Destination
description: Assignment & Grading Service may improperly store or share student data with unauthorized parties, leading to privacy violations.

title: Data Integrity Compromise
description: Student data could be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during processing at the Assignment & Grading Service, affecting grading accuracy and student records.

title: Unnecessary Data Sharing at Source
description: Portal may share more student data than necessary for the grading request, increasing exposure risk and potential for identification.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Assignments
description: The Assignment Store (DS1) receives and stores sensitive student assignment data including student ID, course, and submission time. Without proper access controls, unauthorized parties could access this data, potentially leading to privacy violations.

title: Student Identification from Assignment Data
description: The stored assignment data contains student ID, course, and submission time, which can be used to uniquely identify students and link their academic activities. This creates identification risks if the data is accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: Excessive Data Collection and Storage
description: The Assignment Store collects and retains student ID, course, and submission time with each assignment. This may exceed what is necessary for the grading function, potentially violating data minimization principles.

title: Insecure Data Sharing from Grading Service
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) shares assignment data with the Assignment Store. If the sharing mechanism lacks proper security controls, data could be intercepted or mishandled during transmission.

title: Linkability of submission metadata
description: Meta-data about which submissions are being reviewed in the queue could be used to link students to their submissions and infer enrollment patterns or course participation.

title: Identification through submission request
description: The teacher's request for the submission queue could reveal which students are enrolled in their courses, potentially exposing student enrollment information.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submissions
description: The Grades Portal Web App could expose student submission data to unauthorized parties through improper access controls or data leakage during the review process.

title: Teacher identity usurpation
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate a teacher to gain unauthorized access to student submissions if authentication mechanisms are compromised.

title: Identification of Students via Submission Data
description: The portal shares student names with work content and submission times, directly identifying individual students to the teacher. This creates a risk that student identities could be exposed beyond intended purposes.

title: Linkability of Student Information
description: Student names combined with work content and submission times allow linking of multiple data points about the same student, potentially enabling profiling or correlation of student activities across different contexts.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Data
description: The teacher, as the destination, may have access to student submission data beyond their authorized role, potentially leading to unauthorized sharing or misuse of student information.

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Student Submissions
description: Submission times are recorded but may not provide sufficient audit trail to prevent denial of submission by students or teachers, affecting accountability.

title: Student Identification via Feedback Text
description: Written feedback text may contain identifying information about the student or teacher, enabling identification of individuals through the data flow.

title: Linkability of Student Records
description: Student ID combined with grade and feedback data could be used to link this record to other student records, creating a comprehensive profile of the student.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grades and Feedback
description: The Grades Portal Web App may store grades and feedback in a way that allows unauthorized access, potentially exposing sensitive student performance data.

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Grading Actions
description: If the system does not properly log and authenticate grading actions, teachers could deny having submitted grades or feedback.

title: Excessive Data Collection by Teacher
description: The teacher may share more data than necessary (e.g., grader ID) when recording grades, potentially exposing unnecessary information.

title: Unauthorized Identification of Students from Grade Records
description: Grade records stored in DS2 contain student IDs, course information, and grades. If the database is accessed by unauthorized parties, students could be identified and their academic performance exposed.

title: Disclosure of Sensitive Grade Information
description: Grade records contain sensitive academic information including grades and feedback. Improper access controls at the destination could lead to unauthorized disclosure of this private information to individuals without legitimate need to know.

title: Linkability of Student Data Across Courses
description: The data flow contains student IDs, course information, and timestamps. This metadata could be used to link a student's performance across different courses and time periods, potentially revealing patterns about their academic behavior.

title: Unauthorized Grading Service Access
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) could be accessed by unauthorized users who could submit or modify grade records, potentially leading to grade manipulation or impersonation of legitimate graders.

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Grading Actions
description: While grader IDs are recorded, if the system does not properly authenticate and log grading actions, graders could potentially deny having submitted grades, and students could dispute grades without verifiable evidence.

title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: Student's personal identity information is shared with the Grades Portal Web App when requesting grades, potentially exposing identifiable information to the system.

title: Unauthorized Grade Disclosure
description: Grades and feedback data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the Grades Portal Web App lacks proper access controls and authentication mechanisms.

title: Grade Data Manipulation
description: Grades and feedback data could be altered or tampered with by unauthorized actors if the Grades Portal Web App lacks adequate data integrity controls.

title: Grade Data Linkability
description: Grades data in transit could be linked with other personal data to create a comprehensive profile of the student, potentially revealing sensitive information.

title: Unauthorized interception of grades and feedback during transmission
description: Grades and teacher feedback transmitted from the portal to the student could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission if the communication channel is not properly secured (e.g., lacking TLS encryption).

title: Linkability through metadata in transit
description: Metadata about the data flow (e.g., timing, packet size, destination IP) could be used by an observer to link the student to other data or activities, potentially revealing patterns about the student's academic performance or behavior.

title: Tampering with grades and feedback during transmission
description: Grades and teacher feedback could be altered or tampered with during transmission, compromising data integrity and potentially leading to incorrect academic records or misleading feedback.

title: Improper disclosure of student data at source
description: The portal system may improperly disclose student grades and feedback to unauthorized parties before transmission, such as through logging, debugging, or improper access controls within the system.

title: Unauthorized disclosure by student recipient
description: The student may share their grades and teacher feedback with unauthorized parties (e.g., peers, employers, or family members) after receiving them, potentially violating privacy expectations or academic policies.

title: Linkability of Parent-Child Account Relationship
description: Metadata about the parent-child account linkage in the data flow could be used to link the parent to the child, potentially revealing the child's identity to unauthorized observers monitoring the data flow.

title: Identification of Child Through Grades Data
description: The grades portal processes and stores child's grades, which could be used to identify the child, especially if combined with other information or if the grades are accessible to unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child's Grades
description: The grades portal may store or process the child's grades in a way that exposes them to unauthorized parties, such as through inadequate access controls or data breaches.

title: Usurpation of Parent's Identity
description: If the parent's authentication mechanism is weak, an attacker could impersonate the parent and access the child's grades, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive educational information.

title: Identification of Child through Academic Data
description: The Grades Portal Web App shares child's grades, feedback, and submission history with the parent. This data is inherently identifying as it is tied to a specific student, potentially revealing the child's identity to unauthorized parties if the parent's access is compromised.

title: Linkability of Child's Academic Information
description: The shared academic data (grades, feedback, submission history) can be linked with other data sources to create a comprehensive profile of the child, potentially revealing patterns in academic performance, behavioral issues, or other sensitive information.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Data in transit between the Grades Portal Web App and the parent could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if the communication channel is not properly encrypted, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive academic information.

title: Unauthorized Access by Impersonated Parent
description: The parent receiving the data could be impersonated by an unauthorized party who gains access to the parent's account, leading to unauthorized viewing of the child's academic information.

title: Data Tampering by Parent
description: The parent receiving the data could alter or tamper with the academic information (grades, feedback, submission history) before storing or using it, leading to data integrity issues.

title: Unauthorized access to stored account records
description: The account directory stores sensitive account records and parent-child relationship links that could be accessed by unauthorized parties, potentially revealing personal information about individuals and their family relationships.
assumptions: The account directory is accessible to parties beyond authorized grading service personnel.

title: Identification of individuals through account records
description: The grading service writes account records to the account directory that could be used to identify individuals, potentially exposing personal information.
assumptions: Account records contain personally identifiable information that can be used to identify individuals.

title: Data integrity compromised in transit
description: Account records and parent-child relationship links transmitted from the grading service to the account directory could be tampered with during transmission, potentially leading to unauthorized modifications.
assumptions: Data transmission is not adequately protected against tampering.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of parent-child relationships
description: The account directory stores parent-child relationship links that could be accessed by unauthorized parties, potentially revealing sensitive family structure information about individuals.
assumptions: Parent-child relationship data is considered sensitive personal information.

title: Linkage of individuals through family relationships
description: The grading service writes parent-child relationship links to the account directory that could be used to link individuals to their family members, potentially enabling re-identification or inference attacks.
assumptions: Parent-child relationships can be used to link individuals across different data contexts.

title: Identification through Grade Records
description: Grade records contain personally identifiable information that can identify students, parents, and teachers. The act of sharing this data from the database exposes individuals to identification risks.

title: Disclosure of Sensitive Grade Information
description: Grade records are sensitive personal data. Sharing them from the database without proper access controls could lead to unauthorized disclosure of academic performance information.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure at Grading Service
description: The Assignment & Grading Service may process grade records and create views that could be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to disclosure of sensitive student information.

title: Identification through Processed Views
description: The grading service builds student, parent, and teacher views that could be used to identify individuals and link them to their academic records, potentially exposing them to profiling or surveillance.

title: Identification through Data in Transit
description: Grade records transmitted from the database to the grading service could be intercepted, and metadata about the data flow could be used to identify the parties involved.
